title: 2027 Retirement Contribution Limits: 401(k), IRA, TSP
metaDescription: The 2027 401(k) contribution limit is $25,500, with higher catch-ups by age. The IRA limit stays $7,500. Your plan may set a lower deferral cap.
cardBlurb: Compare the 2027 retirement contribution limits with 2026 figures, including catch-ups, IRA income ranges and per-paycheck amounts.
introText:
The 2027 401(k) contribution limit is $25,500, while the individual retirement account (IRA) limit remains $7,500. The [Internal Revenue Service (IRS)](https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/401k-limit-increases-to-25500-for-2027-ira-limit-remains-7500) announced the figures on November 12, 2026. The $25,500 employee deferral limit also applies to 403(b) plans, governmental 457 plans and the federal [Thrift Savings Plan (TSP)](https://www.tsp.gov/).

An eligible participant age 50 or older can generally add an $8,500 catch-up, for a $34,000 annual total. At ages 60 to 63, the higher catch-up is $11,750 instead. Adding that catch-up to the $25,500 deferral limit gives a $37,250 total by our calculation. A plan can set a lower deferral cap than the legal limit, and the plan decides whether to offer catch-up contributions.

sections.heading: 2027 Contribution Limits at a Glance
sections.body:
The table separates the regular limit from catch-ups so you can use the row that matches your age and account.

| Limit | 2026 | 2027 | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Employee deferral: 401(k), 403(b), governmental 457 and TSP | $24,500 | $25,500 | Up $1,000 |
| Catch-up, generally age 50 or older | $8,000 | $8,500 | Up $500 |
| Deferral plus catch-up, generally age 50 or older | $32,500 | $34,000 | Up $1,500 |
| Higher catch-up, ages 60 to 63 | $11,250 | $11,750 | Up $500 |
| Deferral plus higher catch-up, ages 60 to 63, by our calculation | $35,750 | $37,250 | Up $1,500 |
| IRA contribution | $7,500 | $7,500 | Unchanged |
| IRA catch-up, age 50 or older | $1,100 | $1,100 | Unchanged |
| General SIMPLE plan contribution | $17,000 | $17,500 | Up $500 |
| Defined contribution plan limit under section 415(c) | $72,000 | $75,000 | Up $3,000 |
| Roth catch-up wage threshold (the 2027 column is the 2026 threshold that governs 2027 catch-ups) | $150,000 | $155,000 | Up $5,000 |

The $37,250 figure adds the IRS's $25,500 deferral limit and $11,750 higher catch-up. The IRS publishes the catch-up amount but does not give that combined total in its announcement. For the prior year's employee deferral and catch-up figures, use the [2026 401(k) limits guide](/guides/401k-contribution-limits-2026/).

The Roth catch-up threshold row needs a different reading from the contribution rows. Notice 2026-66 describes the $155,000 figure as the 2026 threshold used to determine the designation of certain 2027 catch-up contributions. It is not an amount you can contribute.

sections.heading: 401(k), 403(b), 457 and TSP Deferral Limits for 2027
sections.body:
Employees can defer up to $25,500 in 2027 under the listed 401(k), 403(b), governmental 457 and TSP limits. The 2026 figure was $24,500. That $1,000 increase changes the annual legal ceiling, but an individual plan may cap deferrals below it.

For participants age 50 or older, the general catch-up rises from $8,000 to $8,500. Adding $8,500 to $25,500 produces the $34,000 total stated by the IRS. The corresponding 2026 total was $32,500, so the combined amount rises $1,500. Ask the plan administrator whether catch-up contributions are available before setting a payroll election that assumes the full amount.

Employees ages 60, 61, 62 and 63 have a higher $11,750 catch-up instead of the $8,500 general catch-up. It was $11,250 in 2026. By our calculation, $25,500 plus $11,750 equals $37,250 for 2027. The same addition gives $35,750 for 2026, a $1,500 difference between the two totals.

The separate $75,000 defined contribution plan limit under section 415(c) rises from $72,000 in 2026. The [2026 401(k) limits guide](/guides/401k-contribution-limits-2026/) describes that limit as covering employee deferrals and employer contributions, including a match or profit sharing. Do not use $75,000 as an employee-only payroll deferral target. The employee deferral figure in the first row of the table is $25,500 before an applicable catch-up.

Roth and Traditional 401(k) employee contributions share one deferral limit. Splitting an election between the two does not create a second $25,500 allowance. Federal employees comparing plan features can use the [TSP vs 401(k) comparison](/compare/tsp-vs-401k/). The IRS lists both under the same 2027 employee deferral figure.

sections.heading: Roth Catch-Up Wage Threshold for 2027
sections.body:
The $155,000 Roth catch-up wage threshold is used to determine whether certain 2027 catch-up contributions must be designated Roth. [IRS Notice 2026-66](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/n-26-66.pdf) states:

"The Roth catch-up wage threshold for 2026, which under section 414(v)(7)(A) is used to determine whether an individual's catch-up contributions to an applicable employer plan (other than a plan described in section 408(k) or (p)) for 2027 must be designated as Roth contributions, is increased from $150,000 to $155,000."

This threshold applies to catch-up contributions only. The notice excludes plans described in section 408(k) or (p), including simplified employee pension and SIMPLE plans. Whether an employer plan offers Roth contributions is plan-specific. Ask the plan administrator what catch-up elections the plan permits before choosing a designation.

Keep the threshold separate from the contribution amount. The $25,500 figure is the regular 2027 employee deferral limit. The $155,000 figure is the threshold identified in the notice for the catch-up designation.

sections.heading: IRA Limits and Income Phase-Outs for 2027
sections.body:
The 2027 IRA contribution limit stays at $7,500, and the age-50 catch-up stays at $1,100. Together, those two amounts equal $8,600 for someone eligible for the catch-up. Unlike the unchanged contribution amounts, several income phase-out ranges rise from 2026 to 2027.

| Income phase-out range | 2026 | 2027 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Traditional IRA deduction: single taxpayer covered by a workplace plan | $81,000 to $91,000 | $83,000 to $93,000 |
| Traditional IRA deduction: married filing jointly, contributing spouse covered | $129,000 to $149,000 | $133,000 to $153,000 |
| Traditional IRA deduction: contributor not covered, spouse covered | $242,000 to $252,000 | $250,000 to $260,000 |
| Traditional IRA deduction: married filing separately and covered | $0 to $10,000 | $0 to $10,000 |
| Roth IRA contribution: single or head of household | $153,000 to $168,000 | $158,000 to $173,000 |
| Roth IRA contribution: married filing jointly | $242,000 to $252,000 | $250,000 to $260,000 |
| Roth IRA contribution: married filing separately | $0 to $10,000 | $0 to $10,000 |

The Traditional IRA rows describe deduction phase-outs under the workplace-coverage conditions named in each row. If neither spouse is covered by a retirement plan at work, those deduction phase-outs do not apply. The Roth IRA rows describe contribution income phase-outs, so do not treat a Traditional IRA deduction range as the Roth contribution range for the same filing status.

The [2026 IRA limits guide](/guides/ira-contribution-limits-2026/) provides the prior-year figures for a separate election or tax-year comparison.

Notice 2026-66 lists Saver's Credit income figures of $83,000 for married couples filing jointly, $62,250 for heads of household and $41,500 for singles and married taxpayers filing separately. The corresponding 2026 figures were $80,500, $60,375 and $40,250. The notice says the 2027 figures apply to contributions to ABLE accounts made after December 31, 2026, because Saver's Match replaces the Saver's Credit for elective contributions to qualifying retirement plans and IRAs. Do not use the listed Saver's Credit figures alone to decide how a retirement-plan contribution will be treated.

sections.heading: SIMPLE Plan Limits for 2027
sections.body:
The general SIMPLE retirement account contribution limit rises to $17,500 in 2027 from $17,000 in 2026. Certain applicable SIMPLE accounts have a higher $19,100 limit, up from $18,100. Those are different base amounts, so identify which SIMPLE limit the plan uses before turning an annual target into a payroll election.

The general SIMPLE catch-up for someone age 50 or older remains $4,000. A different $3,850 catch-up applies to certain applicable SIMPLE plans and is also unchanged. For ages 60 to 63, the higher SIMPLE catch-up remains $5,250. These SIMPLE catch-up amounts differ from the $8,500 general catch-up and $11,750 higher catch-up listed for the 401(k), 403(b), governmental 457 and TSP group.

The Roth catch-up wage-threshold sentence in Notice 2026-66 excludes SIMPLE plans. Keep that exclusion separate from the SIMPLE contribution amounts: the SIMPLE limits above still describe how much may be contributed under their stated categories. Ask the plan administrator which base limit and catch-up category apply to the plan before setting an election.

sections.heading: What Maxing Out 2027 Takes Per Paycheck
sections.body:
A $25,500 annual deferral takes $980.77 from each of 26 equal biweekly paychecks, by our calculation. At ModernWallet, we divided each 2027 limit across common pay schedules in our internal calculation to see what maxing out takes from every paycheck. The inputs are the IRS limits and the number of equal pay periods: $25,500 divided by 26 equals $980.77 when rounded to cents.

| 2027 annual deferral target | Weekly, 52 checks | Biweekly, 26 checks | Semimonthly, 24 checks | Monthly, 12 checks |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $25,500, under age 50 | $490.38 | $980.77 | $1,062.50 | $2,125.00 |
| $34,000, generally age 50 or older | $653.85 | $1,307.69 | $1,416.67 | $2,833.33 |
| $37,250, ages 60 to 63, total by our calculation | $716.35 | $1,432.69 | $1,552.08 | $3,104.17 |

Every per-paycheck entry in the table is our calculation, using equal pay periods and the stated annual target. For example, $34,000 divided by 12 gives $2,833.33 per month when rounded. The $37,250 target uses our addition of the IRS's $25,500 deferral limit and $11,750 higher catch-up. Rounding individual paycheck amounts to cents can leave a small difference from the annual target, so use the annual limit when setting the final election.

Some biweekly calendars have 27 paychecks in a calendar year. In that case, our calculation puts $25,500 at $944.44 per check, $34,000 at $1,259.26 and $37,250 at $1,379.63, with each result rounded to cents. Using the 26-check amount for all 27 checks would overshoot the annual target by one paycheck. Count the pay dates in the calendar used for your election rather than assuming that every biweekly year has 26.

A plan with a lower deferral cap calls for a lower annual target than the legal maximum. After choosing the target and counting pay dates, use the [401(k) calculator](/retirement/401k-calculator/) to project how the contribution amount could affect retirement savings.

sections.heading: Our Takeaway for 2027 Elections
sections.body:
The IRS's $25,500 employee deferral limit is the starting figure for a 2027 401(k), 403(b), governmental 457 or TSP election. Eligible participants age 50 or older can generally add $8,500, while ages 60 to 63 have the $11,750 higher catch-up instead. The IRA limit remains $7,500, with an unchanged $1,100 catch-up.

Those legal figures may be higher than an employer plan permits. A plan can cap deferrals below the legal limit and decides whether to offer catch-up contributions. Roth availability is also plan-specific, and Notice 2026-66 sets out a threshold used for certain 2027 catch-up designations. Request the plan's election details from its administrator if any of those conditions could affect the amount entered in payroll.

Someone using a different plan type, including a self-employed saver whose plan is outside the listed deferral categories, should use that plan's document rather than the 401(k) row. For a covered plan, our per-paycheck calculation also changes when a biweekly calendar has 27 checks instead of 26. Compare the plan's permitted amount and the year's pay dates with the 2027 401(k) contribution limit, then update your payroll election.

faqs.question: What is the 401(k) contribution limit for 2027?
faqs.answer: The 2027 employee deferral limit is $25,500. An eligible participant age 50 or older can generally add an $8,500 catch-up, for $34,000 total. At ages 60 to 63, the $11,750 higher catch-up gives a $37,250 total by our calculation, if the plan permits catch-up contributions.

faqs.question: Is the 2027 401(k) limit final or expected?
faqs.answer: The $25,500 figure is an announced 2027 limit, not an estimate. The IRS announced it on November 12, 2026. An individual plan may still set a lower employee deferral cap.

faqs.question: What is the 2027 Roth 401(k) contribution limit?
faqs.answer: Roth and Traditional 401(k) employee contributions share the $25,500 deferral limit. They do not each receive a separate limit. An eligible catch-up may increase the total by age. Notice 2026-66 also states a $155,000 threshold used to determine whether certain 2027 catch-up contributions must be designated Roth.

faqs.question: Is the TSP limit the same as the 401(k) limit for 2027?
faqs.answer: Yes. The IRS lists the TSP with 401(k), 403(b) and governmental 457 plans at a $25,500 employee deferral limit for 2027. The listed catch-ups are generally $8,500 at age 50 or older and $11,750 at ages 60 to 63.

faqs.question: Does the 2027 IRA limit change?
faqs.answer: No. The IRA contribution limit remains $7,500, and the age-50 catch-up remains $1,100. Several Traditional IRA deduction and Roth IRA contribution income phase-out ranges rise for 2027, depending on filing status and workplace-plan coverage.

faqs.question: What is the catch-up limit for ages 60 to 63 in 2027?
faqs.answer: The higher catch-up is $11,750 instead of the general $8,500 catch-up for the listed 401(k), 403(b), governmental 457 and TSP plans. Adding $11,750 to the $25,500 employee deferral limit gives $37,250 by our calculation, if the plan permits the catch-up.
